verdict: Tesla's revenue slipped 3% to $24.9B as deliveries fell 16%, but gross margin widened to 20.1% and energy revenue jumped 25% — a $592M other-expense line, mostly digital-asset losses, held net income to $856M.

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: $3.8B of operating cash flow less $2.4B of capex

segments.name: Automotive
segments.note: Car sales, leasing and regulatory credits — down 11% YoY on 418,227 deliveries, with regulatory credit revenue of $542M vs $692M a year ago.

segments.name: Energy generation and storage
segments.note: Megapack battery systems and solar — up 25% YoY on record storage deployments of 14.2 GWh, the highest quarter yet.

segments.name: Services and other
segments.note: Supercharging, service centers, parts and FSD (supervised-driving) subscriptions — up 18% YoY.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: AI, the Optimus robot, Cybercab and new vehicles — up 40% YoY as Tesla builds out its AI compute and robotaxi infrastructure.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling cars and running the company day to day — up 26% YoY.

opex.name: Restructuring & other
opex.note: Restructuring and other one-off operating charges.

takeaways.title: Deliveries fell
takeaways.text: Tesla delivered 418,227 vehicles, down 16% from a year ago — yet revenue fell only 3%, because energy revenue rose 25%, services rose 18% and average selling prices were higher.

takeaways.title: Margins widened anyway
takeaways.text: Gross margin reached 20.1% — the best in over a year — and automotive gross margin excluding regulatory credits improved to 17.9%, helped by mix and pricing.

takeaways.title: Stock pay swelled
takeaways.text: Stock-based compensation jumped to $954M in the quarter, lifted by the 2025 CEO Performance Award. Excluding stock pay and digital-asset losses, non-GAAP net income was $1,761M ($0.50 a share) vs GAAP net income attributable to common stockholders of $840M ($0.24).

oneTimers: Other expense, net was $592M — mostly a $307M loss on digital assets (Tesla's bitcoin holdings are marked to market each quarter), a swing from the $595M gain in the same quarter a year ago.

Restructuring and other charges of $162M sit inside operating expenses, and stock-based compensation was $954M (vs $579M a year ago), swollen by the 2025 CEO Performance Award — a non-cash cost inside operating expenses.
otherDetail: Interest income of $449M, less $85M of interest expense and $592M of other expense, net — a net -$228M below operating profit.
follow100Note: The rows reconcile to $100 within a cent of rounding.
footerNote: Net income here is Tesla's total net income of $856M; $840M of it is attributable to common stockholders (the rest belongs to minority partners in subsidiaries).
